extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of literary theory; beginning narratologists
extracted.subtask_description: An introductory, systematic account of narratology presenting definitions, core concepts (text, story, fabula), and analytic procedures intended to equip students to describe and interpret narrative texts across media. Emphasizes the use of concepts as heuristic tools for teaching, analysis, and intersubjective discussion rather than as positivistic certainties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narratology as an instrumental/heuristic theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Narratology is conceived as a set of tools, a means to express and specify one’s interpretative reactions to a text; an instrumental view referring to the practice of learning and teaching, not to a claim of objective certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the concepts as intellectual tools for interpretation: they help formulate descriptions that are expressible and discussable. The theory holds no claim to absolute certainty and is useful in varied applications (aesthetic, political criticism, anthropology, visual art, etc.). Beware of treating the theory as a machine that produces knowledge automatically; instead, test definitions against analyses and check consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-part division: text — story — fabula
rubrics_metrics.description: A text is the material/medium in which a story is told; a story is the content of that text and a particular manifestation of a fabula; a fabula is a series of logically and chronologically related events caused or experienced by actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this distinction to separate how events are presented (story/text) from the sequence of events in the imagined world (fabula). Recognize that different texts can realize the same story and fabula differently; the three-part model provides a framework for describing those differences and for systematic analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of text
rubrics_metrics.description: A text is a finite, structured whole composed of signs, which can be linguistic units (words, sentences) or other signs (cinematic shots, painted dots, lines, blots).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize finitude in the sense of identifiable first and last elements of a text, while acknowledging that boundaries are provisional and porous. Use the term broadly to include non-linguistic sign systems when appropriate, but be explicit about the adopted scope in any analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of narrative text
rubrics_metrics.description: A narrative text is a text in which an agent or subject conveys to an addressee ('tells' the reader, viewer, or listener) a story in a medium (language, imagery, sound, buildings, or combinations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identifying narrative texts, attend to the presence of an agent-addressee relation and an act of telling. Make explicit the chosen medium(s) and how they function in conveying the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of story
rubrics_metrics.description: A story is the content of the text and produces a particular manifestation, inflection, and 'colouring' of a fabula.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish the story as the text-specific presentation/shape of events from the fabula's more abstract event-sequence; analyses should specify how textual choices (order, focalization, detail) shape the story's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of fabula
rubrics_metrics.description: A fabula is a series of logically and chronologically related events that are caused or experienced by actors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat fabula as the imagined sequence (memorial trace) that remains with the reader after reading; in analysis, reconstruct the fabula to compare different textual realizations and reader responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event (element of fabula)
rubrics_metrics.description: An event is the transition from one state to another state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify events as state-transitions in fabula reconstructions. Use event-identification to build sequences that clarify causation and chronology in the fabula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actor (element of fabula)
rubrics_metrics.description: Actors are agents that perform actions; they are not necessarily human. To act is defined as to cause or to experience an event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In analysis, be precise about whether an entity is acting (causing) or experiencing; include non-human actors where appropriate and consider how actorhood affects interpretation and sympathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions should be explicit, provisional, and testable
rubrics_metrics.description: Working definitions are provided to empower the student; they are provisional and meant to be tested against analyses and interpretations rather than to claim truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make definitions explicit at the start of an analysis to clarify what is relevant. Use them as a shared vocabulary to facilitate intersubjective discussion; be ready to revise definitions when confronting new texts or arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe the narrative system before examining variations
rubrics_metrics.description: If characteristics of narrative texts can be defined, these characteristics serve as the point of departure for describing how each narrative text is constructed; on that basis one can examine possible variations when the system is concretized into texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First articulate the abstract narrative system (concepts and categories), then apply it to specific texts and examine how texts instantiate, vary, or depart from the system. Expect multiple legitimate descriptions and use the system to make differences discussable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delimit the corpus and clarify terms to avoid circular disputes
rubrics_metrics.description: Determining what counts as part of the corpus (e.g., whether comic strips are narrative texts) depends on agreed definitions (e.g., of 'text') and helps settle disagreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before arguing about inclusion/exclusion, specify the operational definitions you adopt. Clarifying terms prevents circular reasoning and makes disputes resolvable by explicit criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theory as facilitator of intersubjectivity and democratic discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: The concepts are meant to enable users to formulate descriptions that are accessible to themselves and others; systematic theory facilitates discussion by making proposals expressible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the framework to present interpretations as proposals open to critique. Encourage shared terminology to increase intersubjectivity while acknowledging subjective variation in readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Narratology should avoid positivism, reification, and undue taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: The book cautions against positivistic claims, reification of modes as things, and an overly taxonomic approach that mistakes classification for understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize meaningful analytic questions and nuanced interpretation over mere classification. Avoid presenting categories as fixed entities; instead, relate them systematically to the text and cultural context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ask meaningful questions (focus on focalization and reader effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than asking only who speaks or where words come from, narratology should ask what is being proposed for readers to believe, see, feel, or respond to (e.g., the role of focalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame analyses around what the text proposes to the reader and the expected readerly responses (belief, emotion, judgment). Use focalization and narrator figures to explicate how texts guide perception and affect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider narrativity as a cultural mode and narratology as a perspective on culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative is a cultural attitude; narratology is a perspective that implicates text and reading, subject and object, production and analysis, enabling differentiation of the place and effect of narrativity in cultural expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply narratological concepts across media and cultural artefacts without privileging any medium. Analyze the relative importance and effect of narrative segments within broader cultural objects and contexts.
